2608.16515.title: When Context Misleads: Intent-Guided Decoding for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation
2608.16515.paper_summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves large language models by grounding generation in external evidence, but it also introduces a source trust problem: retrieved context may be useful, irrelevant, or even misleading. Existing RAG systems often apply a fixed trust policy toward retrieved evidence, which can either over-trust incorrect context or underuse context when the user explicitly asks for context-following behavior. Therefore, we propose Intent-Guided Decoding (IGD), a framework that arbitrates between retrieved context and parametric memory according to user intent. IGD uses answer-level filtering and token-level correction to steer the final decoding trajectory between retrieved context and parametric memory. We evaluate IGD on three faithful QA benchmarks and three factual-conflict benchmarks across five LLMs, IGD substantially improves factual recovery, achieving gains of up to 65.4 percentage points on factual-conflict benchmarks over Direct RAG, while preserving or improving strict context-following behavior, this findings highlight the importance of balancing factuality and faithfulness in RAG.
2608.16515.paper_summary_zh: 檢索增強生成（RAG）透過將生成基於外部證據來改善大型語言模型，但它也引入了一個來源信任問題：檢索的上下文可能是有用的、無關的，甚至是誤導性的。現有的 RAG 系統通常對檢索的證據應用固定的信任政策，這可能會對不正確的上下文過度信任，或在用戶明確要求上下文跟隨行為時未能充分利用上下文。因此，我們提出了意圖引導解碼（IGD），這是一個根據用戶意圖在檢索的上下文和參數記憶之間進行仲裁的框架。IGD 使用答案級過濾和標記級修正來引導最終的解碼軌跡，介於檢索的上下文和參數記憶之間。我們在三個忠實的 QA 基準和三個事實衝突基準上評估 IGD，IGD 顯著改善了事實恢復，在事實衝突基準上相較於直接 RAG 提高了多達 65.4 個百分點，同時保持或改善了嚴格的上下文跟隨行為，這些發現突顯了在 RAG 中平衡事實性和忠實性的重要性。
